messages:
zoe: user hit 402 on first quickstart call even after adding a card in the console. quick repro attached. :confused:

zoe: repro they ran:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-workspace-OLDabcd...\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-lite\",\"input\":\"hello\"}'
```

zoe: response 402 body: {\"error\":\"payment_required\",\"message\":\"workspace billing inactive\"}

kai: can you paste the org id the user intended to use and the token prefix? sometimes people copy a token from a different org or older sandbox workspace.

zoe: intended org org_New123, token prefix was sk-workspace-OLD... looks like it belonged to another org.

support-bot: token inspection: sk-workspace-OLD... -> owner_org: org_Old999 (billing: active). Provided token is not scoped to org_New123.

kai: diagnosis: quickstart called API with a token that is valid but for a different org; the target org New123 hasn't got billing linked for that token context so API returns 402. Not a webhook race this time.

dev-tools-bot: immediate workaround: create a workspace-scoped token in Settings -> API tokens for org_New123 and retry, or run:
```bash
redwoodctl tokens create --org org_New123 --scope workspace
```

zoe: support created a workspace token for the user and retried: got 200 and expected response. user happy.

sam: follow-up action: add a small quickstart check that validates token->org mapping on startup and prints an actionable error if the token belongs to a different org (suggesting workspace token creation). filing DX-1422. Also update quickstart README with a short note about token scoping.

zoe: closing thread after updating support KB. summary: 402 can mean token-scoped-to-other-org; recommend workspace token for quickstarts. :white_check_mark:
